title: Sparsity of inner product thresholds
statement: Let $n>0$, and consider the Boolean function on pairs of $n$-bit strings that outputs their dot product over $\mathbb F_2$, encoded as a sign. If a real-valued function on the corresponding sign cube represents this function by threshold signs, then it has at least $2^n$ nonzero Fourier coefficients.
hypotheses_covered: the real-valued function is defined on the sign cube of dimension $2n$
it represents the encoded mod-two inner product by threshold signs
